final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced on main (495e1d30), on Linux/amd64 with go1.24.4, the same Go version as the reporter.

**Expected:** two parallel `cmd.Run` calls on separate `*cli.Command`s both finish without an error.
**Actual:** sometimes one of them panics with `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`, the same message the reporter got.
**Trigger:** two goroutines running `Command.Run` at the same time with the default (non-hidden) help. `ensureHelp` resets fields on the single global `HelpFlag` `*BoolFlag` (the "TODO need to remove hack" block, `command_setup.go:203-209`, which sets `hf.value = nil` and more). Meanwhile the other run reads that same object.
**Run:** `go test -run '^Test_run$' -count 100000 -failfast .`
**Reliability:** 11 panicking subtests out of 200,000 subtest runs (5 batches of `-count 20000`; every batch had 1–4). With `-count 100000 -failfast` it failed within about 1s on all 3 tries, on an 8-core VM.
**Artifacts:** `issue_2176_repro_test.go` at the repo root. It is the reporter's test, changed only to use package `cli_test` and to print `debug.Stack()` when it recovers the panic.

Where it panics:
```
(*FlagBase[...]).Get        flag_impl.go:192   (return f.value.Get())
(*Command).Value            command.go:533
(*Command).Bool             flag_bool.go:28
(*Command).checkHelp        command.go:186
(*Command).run              command_run.go:198
```
`go test -race` also flags a write/write data race at `command_setup.go:205`, where two goroutines both run `ensureHelp` on the shared `HelpFlag`.

Likely cause (my reading of the code, not proven): `Get` checks `f.value != nil`, then another run's `ensureHelp` sets `hf.value = nil` before `f.value.Get()` runs. So the nil check and the call race on the one shared flag.

I didn't change any production code.
